claim_text: The foundation says gutenberg.org was hit by vandalism and is being rebuilt
summary: The Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation's own site says gutenberg.org “is undergoing a deep rebuilding due to vandalism”. The same notice was posted on Project Gutenberg's Mastodon account and reported by File 770.
detail: This is the foundation's own wording on a page we read directly. The foundation's “vandalism” is a broad word and does not say what was done.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, the foundation's own site, states it; a news outlet and the project's own social account agree.

claim_text: Outside attackers broke into Project Gutenberg's systems, including root access to a server
summary: The foundation's status updates, as reproduced by File 770, speak of “attackers”, “the chain of exploits used” and “the primary entry into the root access”, and say the site was re-vandalized on Monday.
detail: We read these updates only as File 770 reproduced them, not on Reddit itself. They are the foundation's words, not an outside finding. What was reached, and what data, is not stated.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The foundation's own updates describe unauthorized access and root access; its site confirms vandalism.
notes: The details come from a status thread read second-hand; the core fact (unauthorized intrusion) rests on the foundation's own statements.

claim_text: Code was injected into the site's live pages, and the first guess was a spammer redirecting visitors to a porn site
summary: Updates say injected code was found in static page footers and in catalog front-end links, “looks like a spammer trying to send people to a porn site”. A Nov 16 notice asked users who see an unexpected redirect to report it.
detail: The spammer remark was an early guess, not a conclusion. The foundation later said the traces were “more extensive” than first seen.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Foundation statements relayed by File 770 and the project's feed; nobody outside has checked.

claim_text: Book files appear unaffected: text and EPUB files “seem to be clear”
summary: The Sunday updates say text and EPUB files seem clear and the live HTML pages were targeted. Another says the books are now clear. A later request to mirror operators asks them to report any books containing the text “asiafilm”.
detail: “Seem to be clear” is a hedge, and the later mirror request shows the foundation was still checking. No independent check seen.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reproducing the foundation's updates.

claim_text: The attackers came back on Monday, Nov 16, and vandalized the site again
summary: A Monday 5 AM PT update says gutenberg.org “has been actively re-vandalized by the attackers” and would be offline until further notice. A later one says traces were more extensive than first seen.
detail: Time as given in the foundation's update (8 AM ET). Single reproduction of the update thread.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reproducing the foundation's updates.

claim_text: A likely entry point was found and removed on Tuesday, but the site stays down until the foundation is “100% sure” it is safe
summary: Tuesday 9 PM PT: “A likely source of the primary entry… has been found and is now permanently removed.” Wednesday 4 PM PT: they will not bring the site up until 100% sure it is safe.
detail: The foundation has not named the entry point or any vulnerability.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reproducing the foundation's updates.

claim_text: Project Gutenberg's website went down on Nov 15-16 and, as of 11:39 AM ET on Wednesday, Nov 25, was still down
summary: We loaded gutenberg.org on Nov 25 at 11:39 AM ET and got HTTP 503 and a “Temporarily Down for Maintenance” page. The foundation's site still says the rebuild after vandalism is under way.
detail: Our own check, repeated over several paths and hosts. A search engine's cached copy showed an older “database copy” notice from Nov 15-16, when the site was partly up; that is not the current state. We did not check the file mirrors.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: First-hand check of the site plus the foundation's own notice.

claim_text: ibiblio, which hosts Gutenberg services, reported an unplanned outage of its login and Gutenberg services that began on Nov 15 and was still going on Nov 20
summary: ibiblio staff posted Monday, Nov 16 that login (SSH, SFTP) and Gutenberg services were down, and Nov 18 that it “began on the 15th”. On Nov 20 they said recovery was in a new phase, with next steps by Nov 23.
detail: ibiblio's posts do not say what caused its outage. Its Nov 20 reply to a user asking whether it was a hack said it was constrained by policy and could not give detail.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ibiblio's own support site, a Tier 1 source for its own outage.

claim_text: The ibiblio outage and the Gutenberg vandalism are the same incident
summary: Both started about Nov 15-16 and ibiblio lists Gutenberg among the down services. The foundation says the “hosting service rebuilds and carefully restores data files”. But neither organization has said they are one event.
detail: ibiblio did not name a cause, said its scope includes “an outside entity”, and advised users who reuse their login password elsewhere to change it. That suggests a security event but is not a statement.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The timing and wording fit but no source states it.
notes: Keep this separate from c001-c002 unless a source connects them.

claim_text: ibiblio told users who reuse their login password elsewhere to change it
summary: On Nov 19 an ibiblio staff post said that people who use the same password for their ibiblio login anywhere else should change it now.
detail: This is advice to ibiblio users. It does not say passwords were taken, and it does not mention Project Gutenberg accounts.
label: Confirmed

summary: The foundation's updates call the attackers “attackers” and “vandals” but name no one. No group has claimed it in any source we read.
detail: The early “spammer” guess was never confirmed. We did not look at leak sites or underground forums.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source names an actor or motive.

claim_text: User data or personal information was exposed
summary: No source says any data was taken. The foundation has not discussed data exposure.
detail: Silence is not a finding. The foundation has not given a scope of what was reached.
label: Not established

claim_text: The foundation said on Nov 25 the website should be back later that afternoon, with its database intact and the books safe
summary: Project Gutenberg's Mastodon account posted at 10 AM UTC on Nov 25 that the website should be back later that afternoon (US Eastern time), that its database is intact and the books are safe, and that it is rebuilding the site.
detail: A post on a social platform, so Tier 4, though from the foundation's own account. It is an expectation, not a return. 'Database intact' does not say whether anything was read or copied.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The post states the expected return, the intact database and the safe books.
